brief: A planter of four cells with a water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell.

requirements.evidence: Four full bases (piece:0..3,0,0), each with a hex-bin-third-drain bin filled with soil and planted (prop:1-4).

requirements.requirement: Water pipe running through the bases
requirements.evidence: Pipe run-1, set to irrigation mode, enters the base at (0,0) and runs straight through (1,0), (2,0) and (3,0).

The run passes under all four planted bins, and each bin is a drain bin. The configurator only checks how parts fit, so it can't confirm that water actually reaches each bin or that the pipe doesn't leak. Watertightness depends on the print material.

finish.summary: I built a planter from four full hex bases set in a straight row, cells (0,0) to (3,0). One irrigation pipe run (run-1) goes straight through all four bases. Because a pipe passes through each base, the configurator only allows third-depth bins there, so each cell has a shallow third-depth drain bin. All four bins are filled with soil and planted. Every open face has an end cap, and the joints between bases are bolted. The configurator check shows no issues and no mesh clashes. It only checks fit, so whether the parts hold water depends on the print material and was not checked.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 1 run IRRIGATION: non-potable supply. Corners are flexible hose, glued into Sch 40 sockets, one coupling wherever hose meets rigid pipe.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
